question: Which law was based on notes of the music?
solution:
The correct answer is the __**Law of octaves**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **​Law of octaves was based on notes of the music.**
 
• The 56** elements** that were known at the time were attempted by **British scientist John Newlands in 1864.**
 
• Based on their **atomic masses**, he sorted them in ascending order and saw that every **eighth element** shared comparable characteristics. This observation led to the formulation of **Newland's law of octaves.**
 
• According to the** law of octaves,** every eighth element possesses characteristics that are identical when the elements are ordered in ascending **order of atomic mass.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Newton law**

 
 
• ​According to **Newton's first law of motion**, an external force must be applied in order for an object to begin** moving, stop moving, or change direction.**
 
• **Inertia **is the ability of large entities to resist changes in their **state of motion**. The **law of inertia** is another name for the **first law of motion.**
 
 
 
• **Mendeleev law**
 
 
• ​**Mendeleev **organised the elements in** horizontal rows**, increasing the order of their** atomic masses** until he discovered an element whose characteristics matched those of the **first element. **
 
 
 
• **Modern periodic law**
 
 
• ​According to the **Modern Periodic Law, **an element's chemical and physical characteristics are periodic functions of its** atomic number.**
 
• The elements with** identical properties** reoccur after predetermined regular intervals if elements are put in increasing **atomic number sequence.**
